summary: Ephemeral allocator shadowing from analytics sidecar causing dedicated throughput flicker and short GPU attach timeouts
description: Issue summary: NimbleDocs reported repeated short-duration throughput dips (10-60s) on their dedicated pool causing p50->p99 latency divergence and occasional request timeouts (504/429) between 2026-03-09T22:10Z and 2026-03-10T03:00Z. Impact: Customer sees degraded SLA for high-throughput embedding and chat routes; user-facing errors and retry storms. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west, pinned to llama-13b-quantized-v2. Observed behavior: regular baseline throughput, then periodic 20-40s windows where GPU attach latency increases, batcher serialization increases, and autoscaler briefly sheds small numbers of slots. Root suspicion: a background analytics sidecar (customer metrics collector / internal sampler) is intermittently triggering heavy allocator activity that shadows the tenant's slot allocator, causing ephemeral slot reservation/lease churn ("allocator shadowing") and prefetch/pipeline resonance that looks like noisy-neighbor behavior. This produces transient GPU shortages despite overall capacity headroom.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NimbleDocs dedicated pool configuration (pinned model llama-13b-quantized-v2) in us-west.
2) Generate a sustained medium fanout workload: ~200 concurrent short requests (context length 512) with bursts to 500 QPS for 30s every 5 minutes.
3) Enable the analytics sidecar sampling at default interval (customerside default sample window enabled).
4) Observe allocator and attach metrics on affected nodes and the customer's per-route latency dashboards during the burst windows.
logs: [2026-03-10T00:12:23Z] serving-runtime: gpu_attach_timeout route=/v1/generate tenant=NIMBLEDOCS status=504 attach_wait=350ms
investigation_notes: Initial triage: correlated p99 spikes with a consistent 200-400ms increase in allocator lease acquire time across machines hosting the customer's reserved slice.

Telemetry: node-level NVMe IO and nvlink metrics were normal; CPU soft-avail on nodes hosting sidecar collector spiked during the windows, suggesting sidecar CPU and epoll wakeups were adding scheduling jitter.
Reproduced in staging: enabling the sidecar sampler with high-frequency histogram upload produced the same short attach delays and autoscaler decisions in a synthetic dedicated pool testbed.

Hypothesis: analytics sidecar opens many short-lived connections to the local prefetched metadata store and triggers allocator heartbeat jitter. The allocator treats the high short-lived reservation volume as noise, causing temporary lease delays and small autoscaler contractions; this manifests as ephemeral GPU shortages for active tenants.

Cross-references: Slack thread #support-nimbledocs (https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C03SUPPORT/p167850), related incident SUP-215007 (midday-throughput-lull-dedicated-pool) and linked internal INT-12901 which added recent sidecar sampler changes.

Quant metrics: p99 latency increased from 420ms -> 1.9s during windows; attach_wait median increased 40ms -> 360ms; slot_available metric dropped by 6% for ~30s windows despite overall <80% GPU utilization.
comments: Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-10: Logged initial customer report, requested ACL-limited logs and timeline. Asked customer to confirm any local analytics sampling toggles.
Customer (NimbleDocs, Alex Rivera) 2026-03-10: Confirmed sidecar sampling was recently enabled by their infra team to improve telemetry fidelity.
SRE (Diego Ramos) 2026-03-11: Deployed a staging reproducer and saw attach_wait spike when sidecar sampling rate set to <=3s. Lower sampling (>=30s) removed the effect.

Eng (Priya Singh) 2026-03-11: Noted allocator code treats connection surge events as prefetch requests and briefly rebalances cache leases. Proposed a quick guard: add back-pressure / sampling rate circuit to sidecar and a short debounce in allocator lease handling.
Support (Maya Chen) 2026-03-12: Customer applied temporary mitigation (lower sidecar rate) and reports significant improvement; awaiting engineering patch roll out.
resolution_notes: Workaround applied: NimbleDocs lowered analytics sidecar sampling from 2s -> 45s which eliminated the transient attach spikes. Engineering action items: (1) Deploy allocator debounce patch to ignore short-lived sampling-driven reservation spikes (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1486), (2) Add a sidecar best-practice note to dedicated onboarding docs suggesting sampling <=30s for high-throughput tenants, (3) Add an autoscaler signal to account for short attach jitter so it doesn't prematurely shrink tiny deltas. Rollout plan: debounce patch in canary 2026-03-13, full rollout 2026-03-15 after smoke tests. Follow-up: schedule a postmortem run 1 week after rollout to verify recurrence and update customer SLA remediation if needed.
